bull_bear.body: ICONIQA’s ₹6.35cr Ind AS charge is a non-cash accounting distortion — actual cash outflow for lease is ₹0 in Q2 (rent-free period); the real cash flow strength is hidden in normalized PAT of ₹12.65cr; Regenta Z franchise model has near-zero capex and 3x faster ROI than owned hotels
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Explicit return hurdle: "Rigorous investment management metrics — We continue to focus on +20% ROCE", listed as one of the three drivers of Vision 2030.
- Capital intensity is deliberately pushed to third parties — "focus on management contracts and franchising to scale efficiently" — with owned/JV keys essentially flat over FY22-FY26 while managed/franchise keys more than doubled.
- Consolidated balance sheet at FY26 shows the IND-AS lease build-up: right-of-use assets ₹553.4 Cr (vs ₹104.6 Cr in FY25) against non-current lease liabilities ₹529.5 Cr and current lease liabilities ₹13.2 Cr; total assets ₹1,041.6 Cr (FY25: ₹538.2 Cr).
- Conventional debt remains modest relative to leases: FY26 non-current borrowings ₹82.5 Cr and current borrowings ₹15.5 Cr, with total equity ₹275.5 Cr; assets held-for-sale of ₹24.0 Cr sit on the FY26 balance sheet.
- The deck makes no mention of dividends, buybacks or a stated payout policy.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "A HOUSE OF BRANDS" / "A HOTEL BRAND FOR EVERY PERSONALITY": a brand ladder spanning upscale (Iconiqa), boutique with local experiences, warm midscale, youthful value-priced modern, and "the everywhere budget hotel brand" — the deck's competitive advantage slide cites "Versatile Asset Portfolio a brand for every personality".
- Competitive advantage is framed as a "Balanced portfolio having presence in over 85+ locations and 19 states" plus "Strong Sales Presence across major source markets in India" (100+ sales force, 8500+ employees).
- Royal Orchid "owns, leases, manages and franchises properties, running the entire operation from rooms to food & beverage, banquets to outdoor caterings" — business structure split by legal entity (ROHL + subsidiaries) and by portfolio (owned / leased / managed & franchised).
- "WHAT WILL DRIVE VISION 2030" names three pillars: clearly defined Brand Architecture, Smart Execution ("Iconiqa, Mumbai – 12 months from shell to completion") and Return on Invested Capital; "ICONIQA is the foundation for Vision 2030".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Iconiqa ramp] Iconiqa Mumbai is presented as a separate P&L block: "Q1 Total Income: ₹20.1 CR | Target Annual Run-rate: ₹80-100 CR", and "Iconiqa gets rated as No 1 hotel on Trip Advisor in Mumbai within 4 months of operation". The deck also reports Q1 FY27 cash profit and PAT "Excluding Iconiqa", i.e. the asset is still dilutive at the reported level.
- [IND-AS 116 distortion] "The adoption of IND-AS led to a notional increase in depreciation and finance costs of Rs. 20.2 CR, resulting in a reduction in PAT of Rs. 3.4 CR at the Consolidated level for the quarter ended June 2026"; at standalone the notional increase was Rs. 5.7 CR for a Rs. 0.2 CR PAT reduction. The deck presents every table on both With-INDAS and Without-INDAS bases.
- [Subsidiary lease recognition] "Royal Orchid Mumbai Private Limited, one of the subsidiary company, has recognized its Right-of-Use (ROU) assets and corresponding lease liabilities. Consequently, the subsidiary has recorded depreciation and finance cost of Rs 13.4 cr in the current quarter ended June 2026 & 32.5 cr in financial year ended March 2026."
- [Pre-operating write-off] "Pre operating expenditure of Rs 5.50 CR has been written off during the 4th quarter 2025-26 and financial year ended March 2026."
- [Conflicting hotel-count targets] The deck states three different long-term network ambitions: "345+ Hotels" by FY30 (Vision 2030 slide), "Vision to grow to 200+ hotels" (Phase 2 slide), and "Our Vision is to operate 350+ profitable and responsible hotels" (ROHL Vision slide). Both/all readings are reproduced rather than reconciled.

business.body: Royal Orchid Hotels operates and manages hotels and resorts across India (and select overseas locations) primarily through an asset-light model of management contracts and franchises. Its brand portfolio spans Royal Orchid (upscale), Regenta (midscale, the group's core brand), the newly launched Iconiqa (upscale lifestyle), plus boutique, value and budget offerings, serving business and leisure travellers with rooms, food & beverage outlets and banqueting/event spaces.

outlook.body: 38 signed hotels: 2 Crestoria (40 keys each), 1 Regenta Resort (Dodamarg), 1 Regenta (Gurgaon Sector 20, 120 keys), 1 Regenta (Lucknow, 172 keys), rest Regenta Z (40-60 keys each)

outlook.body: Franchise-led Regenta Z expansion (40-60 key hotels) enables 2x faster scaling than owned assets; potential M&A of weaker regional chains to accelerate footprint; F&B monetization via standalone concepts; international expansion via franchise model post-2027
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Accelerate the opening of pipeline hotels to drive revenue and operating leverage.
- Diversify the portfolio with new brand concepts and upscale offerings.
- Pursue digital transformation for personalized guest journeys and efficiency.
- Scale via the asset-light model (management contracts and franchises) with focus on Tier-2/3 cities and high-potential gateway destinations.
- Maintain financial discipline while pursuing high-ROCE opportunities.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The company expanded its hotel portfolio during FY26, adding multiple properties and maintaining a signed pipeline of 52+ hotels in various stages of signing and execution. The key highlight was the launch of Iconiqa at Mumbai International Airport T2, marking entry into the upscale lifestyle segment; the commissioning of new properties (including Iconiqa Mumbai) drove higher interest and depreciation expense in the year. Expansion continues via the asset-light model (management contracts and franchises), with focus on Tier-2/3 cities and high-potential gateway destinations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian hospitality industry outlook described as positive, supported by economic growth, rising disposable incomes, infrastructure improvements and increasing tourism.
- Improved occupancies, better Average Room Rates (ARR), and higher contributions from food & beverage and banqueting segments cited as revenue growth drivers.
- Management expects margin expansion as newly commissioned properties mature.
- New property commissioning and strategic investments (including Iconiqa Mumbai) increased interest and depreciation expense in the short term, which management frames as building future earnings potential.
- Strong pipeline of 52+ hotels in various stages of signing and execution.

segment_detail.body: ICONIQA Mumbai: 292 keys, ₹3cr revenue in Q2, ₹5cr OpEx, targeting ₹100cr+ ARR next year; Regenta: 70% occupancy, 54% managed segment occupancy; Regenta Z: franchise model, low capex, rapid scale; F&B: 40% of revenue, undergoing strategic revamp; Corporate/leisure mix: 60:40, domestic guests up 14k YoY

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Upscale:** Royal Orchid, Iconiqa
- **Midscale:** Regenta
- **Boutique:** Regenta Central / Regenta Place formats
- **Value:** Regenta Inn
- **Budget:** value/budget branded properties

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India hospitality (Tier-2/3 cities and gateway destinations)
- overseas hotels (international presence noted in risk management framework)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: 38 signed hotels: 2 Crestoria (40 keys each), 1 Regenta Resort (Dodamarg), 1 Regenta (Gurgaon Sector 20, 120 keys), 1 Regenta (Lucknow, 172 keys), rest Regenta Z (40-60 keys each)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: >15% FY27 (driven by ICONIQA full year + 38 new keys); Margin: EBITDA margin target 25%+ by FY27; Order inflow: 38 signed hotels to commission by 2027; Capex/commissioning: ₹150-200cr FY27 for 5 new revenue-share hotels (Gurgaon, Lucknow, North Goa, Crestoria, Regenta Z)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Franchise-led Regenta Z expansion (40-60 key hotels) enables 2x faster scaling than owned assets; potential M&A of weaker regional chains to accelerate footprint; F&B monetization via standalone concepts; international expansion via franchise model post-2027

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian hospitality industry outlook described as positive, supported by economic growth, rising disposable incomes, infrastructure improvements and increasing tourism.
- Improved occupancies, better Average Room Rates (ARR), and higher contributions from food & beverage and banqueting segments cited as revenue growth drivers.
- Management expects margin expansion as newly commissioned properties mature.
- New property commissioning and strategic investments (including Iconiqa Mumbai) increased interest and depreciation expense in the short term, which management frames as building future earnings potential.
- Strong pipeline of 52+ hotels in various stages of signing and execution.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Employee cost: ₹25cr/quarter (₹3cr from ICONIQA pre-op); rent cost: ₹5.7cr/quarter (ex-ICONIQA); ICONIQA OpEx: ₹4-4.5cr/month; EBITDA margin: 24% ex-ICONIQA, 20% consolidated; cost leverage expected as new hotels stabilize and AI reduces labor dependency

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing franchise expansion (Regenta Z) over owned assets; debt used for lease commitments; no dividend policy stated; focus on cash ROCE >25%; no equity raise planned; F&B and tech investments funded from ops

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company expanded its hotel portfolio during FY26, adding multiple properties and maintaining a signed pipeline of 52+ hotels in various stages of signing and execution. The key highlight was the launch of Iconiqa at Mumbai International Airport T2, marking entry into the upscale lifestyle segment; the commissioning of new properties (including Iconiqa Mumbai) drove higher interest and depreciation expense in the year. Expansion continues via the asset-light model (management contracts and franchises), with focus on Tier-2/3 cities and high-potential gateway destinations.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, execution-focused, and disciplined; repeated emphasis on speed, cost control, and asset-light scalability; management visibly proud of ICONIQA’s 11-month delivery; tone is long-term builder, not short-term speculator

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": "true", "note": "NCLT petition under Companies Act Sections 241 and 242 (disclosed to exchanges March 02, 2024; case details on NCLT portal) and an Interim Order cum Show Cause Notice issued by SEBI — both referenced in the notes to standalone/consolidated financial statements and cited as the basis for a Qualified Opinion by the statutory auditor (Board's Report, Corporate Governance Report).", "as_of": "2026-09-04"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- brand: Multi-brand portfolio spanning five price points (upscale, boutique, midscale, value, budget) under Royal Orchid, Regenta and Iconiqa — evidence: "FIVE BRANDS ... A brand for every price point" covering upscale, boutique, midscale, value and budget segments.
- distribution: Asset-light management-contract and franchise model enabling rapid scale-up with a large signed pipeline — evidence: "a strong pipeline of 52+ hotels in various stages of signing and execution" [planned]

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Land-use delays (Goa renovation); wage inflation in hospitality labor; lease renegotiation risk for ICONIQA; occupancy volatility in Goa due to taxi regulations; competition from Marriott, IHG in upscale segment; Ind AS accounting distortion masking true cash flow

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: ICONIQA’s ₹6.35cr Ind AS charge is a non-cash accounting distortion — actual cash outflow for lease is ₹0 in Q2 (rent-free period); the real cash flow strength is hidden in normalized PAT of ₹12.65cr; Regenta Z franchise model has near-zero capex and 3x faster ROI than owned hotels

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Accelerate the opening of pipeline hotels to drive revenue and operating leverage.
- Diversify the portfolio with new brand concepts and upscale offerings.
- Pursue digital transformation for personalized guest journeys and efficiency.
- Scale via the asset-light model (management contracts and franchises) with focus on Tier-2/3 cities and high-potential gateway destinations.
- Maintain financial discipline while pursuing high-ROCE opportunities.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High capex and long payback for owned upscale hotels | Royal Orchid Hotels Ltd | beneficiary | High | Asset-light model reduces capital intensity and improves ROCE vs peers like Indian Hotels Co |
| Labor cost inflation in hospitality | Budget hotel chains without AI or training systems | loser | Medium | ROHL’s AI-driven ops and in-house GM training create sustainable cost advantage |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Iconiqa ramp] Iconiqa Mumbai is presented as a separate P&L block: "Q1 Total Income: ₹20.1 CR | Target Annual Run-rate: ₹80-100 CR", and "Iconiqa gets rated as No 1 hotel on Trip Advisor in Mumbai within 4 months of operation". The deck also reports Q1 FY27 cash profit and PAT "Excluding Iconiqa", i.e. the asset is still dilutive at the reported level.
- [IND-AS 116 distortion] "The adoption of IND-AS led to a notional increase in depreciation and finance costs of Rs. 20.2 CR, resulting in a reduction in PAT of Rs. 3.4 CR at the Consolidated level for the quarter ended June 2026"; at standalone the notional increase was Rs. 5.7 CR for a Rs. 0.2 CR PAT reduction. The deck presents every table on both With-INDAS and Without-INDAS bases.
- [Subsidiary lease recognition] "Royal Orchid Mumbai Private Limited, one of the subsidiary company, has recognized its Right-of-Use (ROU) assets and corresponding lease liabilities. Consequently, the subsidiary has recorded depreciation and finance cost of Rs 13.4 cr in the current quarter ended June 2026 & 32.5 cr in financial year ended March 2026."
- [Pre-operating write-off] "Pre operating expenditure of Rs 5.50 CR has been written off during the 4th quarter 2025-26 and financial year ended March 2026."
- [Conflicting hotel-count targets] The deck states three different long-term network ambitions: "345+ Hotels" by FY30 (Vision 2030 slide), "Vision to grow to 200+ hotels" (Phase 2 slide), and "Our Vision is to operate 350+ profitable and responsible hotels" (ROHL Vision slide). Both/all readings are reproduced rather than reconciled.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
